articles.headline: Pavin Smith's game-ending homer gives D-backs playoff hope
articles.description: Pavin Smith, a former highly-touted prospect who was waived by the Diamondbacks two months ago, may have saved Arizona's season with a walk-off homer vs. the Yankees to stay alive in the wild card race.
articles.body:
PHOENIX -- Torey Lovullo has said the same phrase several times over the past seven years, even as fans and sometimes reporters rolled their eyes at the Arizona Diamondbacks manager's optimism.

"Pavin Smith can hit," Lovullo would say.

And on Saturday night, he finally did, injecting some life into the D-backs' slim playoff hopes by smacking a game-ending, two-run homer in the ninth inning for a 5-3 win over the New York Yankees. Entering as a pinch-hitter, the left-hander ripped a cutter from Michael Fulmer over the right-field wall.

The D-backs pulled within four games of Philadelphia for the final NL wild card with seven games remaining.

"I'm never looking to be proven right," Lovullo said. "I'm just trying to put players in the best position to be successful and when they have success I share it with them. But I do believe Pavin can hit."

Smith has had an up-and-down career with the D-backs after being selected with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2017 amateur draft after a stellar three seasons in college at Virginia. He has a career batting average of .241 with 47 homers, but has been worth exactly 0.0 wins above replacement, according to baseball-reference.com.

The 30-year-old looked like he might finally be ready for his breakout season this spring, but he developed bone spurs in his elbow in March and needed surgery. That knocked him out of action for roughly two months.

He returned to the lineup on June 1, but looked lost at the plate. The low point came on July 9 when he was designated for assignment by the only organization he had ever known. At the time, he was hitting .141.

Smith cleared waivers, meaning 29 other teams didn't think he was worth picking up. Then the D-backs sent him back to Triple-A Reno, where he slowly regained confidence in his swing.

Now he's making big contributions at a critical stage of the season.

"It felt really good," Smith said. "There were lots of times this year when I didn't feel like I could ever hit again. I think that happens to a lot of people. Just didn't have any timing coming back from the surgery."

Smith's homer was a crowd-pleaser at Chase Field, where a season-high 47,918 fans were in attendance for the franchise's 25-year anniversary celebration of their 2001 World Series win over the Yankees.

Lovullo said their might have been a little magic in the air for the D-backs since so many franchise legends were in the building, including Luis Gonzalez, whose bloop single off Yankees closer and Hall of Famer Mariano Rivera in the ninth inning of Game 7 scored Jay Bell for a 3-2 win.

"Gonzo hit a walk-off about 25 years ago and to be able to do it on the (celebration) night is pretty cool," Smith said. "It's a full stadium. It was a playoff-like atmosphere. Every pitch felt like it mattered more and to pull it out in the end feels good."

articles.headline: Rookie Salas has walk-off single in 10th as Padres beat Marlins 7-6, reduce magic number to 3
articles.description: — Rookie Ethan Salas singled in Jake Cronenworth from third base with one out in the 10th inning and the San Diego Padres beat the Miami Marlins 7-6 on Saturday night to lower their magic number to three for clinching their third straight postseason...
articles.headlineJa: ルーキーのサラスが10回にサヨナラ打、パドレスがマーリンズを7-6で下しマジックナンバーを3に減らす
articles.descriptionJa: 10回裏1死三塁からルーキーのエーザン・サラスがジェイク・クロネンワースを生還させるサヨナラ打を放ち、サンディエゴ・パドレスが土曜夜にマイアミ・マーリンズを7-6で破り、3年連続となるポストシーズン進出決定へのマジックナンバーを3に減らした。
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO -- — Rookie Ethan Salas singled in Jake Cronenworth from third base with one out in the 10th inning and the San Diego Padres beat the Miami Marlins 7-6 on Saturday night to lower their magic number to three for clinching their third straight postseason berth.


              Salas, the Padres' top prospect who was called up Sept. 1, punched a single up the middle on an 0-2 pitch from Josh Ekness (2-4) and his teammates mobbed him in a wild celebration that ended up in the outfield.


              Cronenworth, the automatic runner, advanced on a wild pitch. David Morgan (4-1) got the victory.


              The winning hit came an inning after pinch-hitter Griffin Conine drove a towering, tying homer off Mason Miller with one out in the ninth.


              The Padres won for the 12th time in 13 games and remained tied with the Chicago Cubs at 86-69 for the National League's top wild-card spot, although the Cubs hold the tiebreaker. The Philadelphia Phillies lost 10-3 to the New York Mets to drop a game back. 


              The earliest the Padres can clinch a wild-card spot is Tuesday night at the NL West champion Los Angeles Dodgers.


              Miller was trying for a five-out save when Connine hit a 102-mph four-seamer an estimated 427 feet to right, his 17th.


              Fernando Tatis Jr. tied it at 5 with a solo homer leading off the fourth off Eury Pérez for the Padres, who on Sunday will go for their second sweep of the Marlins this season.


              Ty France then punched an opposite-field double over the outstretched glove of right fielder Esteury Ruiz with two outs in the sixth to bring in Dustin Harris, who was aboard on a one-out opposite field double to left. Harris extended his hitting streak to nine games. 


              The Marlins roughed up Casey Mize through three innings to take a 5-1 lead, including Otto Lopez's two-run home run, his 11th, in the second.


              San Diego's Samad Taylor homered off Pérez in the second, his second, and the Padres scored three in the third, including on Jake Cronenworth's bases-loaded walk.


              Up next
              Marlins RHP Sandy Alcantara (13-10, 3.85 ERA) and Padres RHP Walker Buehler (8-6, 4.58) were scheduled to start Sunday in the series finale.


              ------

articles.headline: Dodgers outslug Giants 10-4, led by Mookie Betts with four hits
articles.description: — Mookie Betts went 4 for 4 with three doubles, Will Smith added three hits including a home run, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 10-4 on Saturday night.
articles.headlineJa: ドジャースがムーキー・ベッツの4安打の活躍でジャイアンツとの打撃戦を10-4で制す
articles.descriptionJa: ムーキー・ベッツが二塁打3本を含む4打数4安打、ウィル・スミスも本塁打を含む3安打を記録し、ロサンゼルス・ドジャースが土曜夜にサンフランシスコ・ジャイアンツを10-4で下した。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- — Mookie Betts went 4 for 4 with three doubles, Will Smith added three hits including a home run, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 10-4 on Saturday night.


              Tommy Edman's two-run, two-out single off reliever Philip Abner snapped a 4-all tie in the fifth. Pinch-hitter Miguel Rojas followed with an RBI single for a 7-4 lead, with Edman thrown out at home to end the inning. 


              Every Dodger had at least one hit, except for struggling Freddie Freeman who was 0 for 5. Betts tied his season high for hits and the team outslugged the Giants, 15-8. The former AL MVP was hitting .249 a week ago, and has since raised his average to .261.


              The Dodgers scored runs in six straight innings to start a game for the first time in 10 years. They've scored 15 runs in their last seven offensive innings, including a four-homer eighth off Abner in Friday's series opener.


              The NL West champions (95-60) won their 95th game to move a season-high 35 games above .500.


              Betts' third double led off the sixth and he scored on Smith's RBI single off reliever Joel Kuhnel. Rookie Josue De Paula added a two-run RBI single, extending the lead to 10-4.


              Three times the Giants rallied to tie the game only to see the Dodgers retake the lead, highlighted by Victor Bericoto's game-tying, 425-foot two-run homer in the third. 


              Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal (11-7) wasn't particularly sharp, allowing four runs and eight hits in five innings. The left-hander struck out three and walked two, with the Dodgers winning each of his last six outings.


              Reliever Edwin Díaz pitched a scoreless eighth in his second straight appearance since coming off the injured list Friday.


              Giants starter Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs and eight hits in 4 2/3 innings with two strikeouts.


              Dodgers right fielder Kyle Tucker fouled a ball off his knee and was replaced by Alex Call in the seventh.


              Up next 
              Neither team had announced their starters for the series finale Sunday.


              ------

articles.headline: Nationals score 4 runs in 11th in an 8-5 victory over the Cardinals
articles.description: — Washington successfully challenged for catcher’s interference with the bases loaded in a four-run 11th inning in the Nationals' 8-5 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals on Saturday night.
articles.headlineJa: ナショナルズが11回に4点を奪いカージナルスに8-5で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜夜に行われたセントルイス・カージナルス戦で、ナショナルズは8-5で勝利した11回表の4得点の場面において、満塁での捕手打撃妨害のアピール（チャレンジ）に成功した。
articles.body:
ST. LOUIS -- — Washington successfully challenged for catcher’s interference with the bases loaded in a four-run 11th inning in the Nationals' 8-5 victory over the St. Louis Cardinals on Saturday night.


              After Washington took the lead on the interference call, Jose Tena had a two-run double and Dylan Crews followed with an RBI sacrifice fly.


              J.J. Wetherholt led off the bottom of the 11th with an RBI single, and St. Louis loaded the bases with no outs, but did not score again. Washington reliever Will Dion got the final out for his first career save.


              Riley Cornelio (3-2) was the winner. Gordon Graceffo (8-2) took the loss.


              The Nationals (73-82) have won six of their last seven following a seven-game losing streak. The Cardinals (75-80) have lost four straight games.


              Jorbit Vivas had a career-high four hits and added an RBI and a run for Washington. James Wood had two hits and scored a run. Daylen Lile blasted a two-run home run to center field in the first inning, the 22nd of the season for the 23-year-old left fielder.


              Nathan Church led off the bottom of the ninth with an infield hit that bounced off the second base bag for a double. Pedro Pages followed with an RBI single to left, his first RBI since June 18, to tie it at 3.


              Vivas hit a two-out RBI single in the 10th inning to give the Nationals a 4-3 lead, only for Mason Wynn to it with an RBI single in the bottom of the inning.


              Up next
              Cardinals LHP Quinn Mathews (2-3, 3.62) was set to face Nationals RHP Jake Irvin (2-9, 5.51) on Sunday in the series finale.

articles.description: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 2 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第2週ベッティングガイド：日曜午後の試合の注目予想
articles.descriptionJa: 当社の専門家が第2週のオッズとプレーヤープロップを深掘りし、ベッティングのヒントとイチオシの賭け枠を提供します。
articles.body:
Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value.

Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league.

From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 1.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

Jump to:

Bowen's Game of the Week | Solak's plays | Walder's props

Bowen's Game of the Week

Cincinnati Bengals at Houston Texans (-2.5, 46.5)

1 p.m. ET on CBS, Reliant Stadium, Houston

This line has fluctuated but at -2.5, I am all-in. Would I feel the same at -3? I wouldn't love it, but I'd be willing to bet Houston at home in a bounce-back game after the Week 1 loss to Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. Let's get into what to look for on both sides of the ball, and we'll finish with some props bets to play.

When Houston has the ball: Houston spent the offseason working on its run game, trading for David Montgomery and adding to the offensive front. And we saw a dedicated effort to run the football in Week 1, as Montgomery had 20 carries, with Woody Marks chipping in with nine. Now, was it super efficient? No. Montgomery averaged just 3.0 YPC, and the Texans registered a run block win rate of 74% (17th in the league). But it's clear that Houston wants the run game to be a foundational element of its offense. This can boost the passing opportunities for quarterback C.J. Stroud, who will see a Bengals defense featuring a rebuilt front anchored by defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II and an underrated secondary that can mix both zone and man looks. I would look for play-action concepts (which mirror the run game) to attack the Bengals' two-deep zone shells while also scheming up some shot plays. With Nico Collins out, the scheme won't change in Houston. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte can work the interior in-breakers while Jaylin Noel operates out of the slot. I truly think Houston looks to control the tempo on offense in this one, but let's keep an eye on third downs because the Texans need to beat man coverage from the Bengals there.

When Cincinnati has the ball: I want to see this matchup against the Texans' defense. Though the Bengals looked flat in a Week 1 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (Joe Burrow finished with 254 yards passing, and Ja'Marr Chase had two receptions for 12 yards), they create conflict because of scheme and talent

articles.headline: NFL Week 2 uniforms: Rams debut 'Classic Sol,' Ravens go all-white
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 2, led by a new alternate look from the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第2週のユニフォーム：ラムズは「クラシック・ソル」を初披露、レイブンズはオールホワイト
articles.descriptionJa: ロサンゼルス・ラムズの新しいオルタネイト・ユニフォームをはじめ、NFL各チームが第2週に着用するユニフォームを紹介。
articles.body:
Uniforms revealed in the offseason will make their respective debuts in Week 2. Fresh from their trip Down Under, the Los Angeles Rams look to win their first game of the season with a design rooted in its history.

Los Angeles will wear its "Classic Sol" alternate threads against the New York Giants on "Monday Night Football." The uniform honors the Rams' championship in 1951, with this season marking the 75th anniversary. A sol-colored jersey includes royal blue stitched and colored numbers. The three-stripe royal blue sleeve design is a direct nod to the uniforms worn in the 1951 season. The Giants will counter by going all-white.

The Baltimore Ravens underwent a closet redesign in the offseason, and with it came a new helmet and combination. Nicknamed "White Noise," Baltimore will pair all-white threads with the "Purple Rising" helmet against the New Orleans Saints. Baltimore originally revealed the purple lids in 2024, but tweaked them in April with a logo change, maintaining the metallic purple. It tops off a sleek new all-white look. 

It's an all-white look for the New York Jets as well, but from head-to-toe. New York unveiled new white helmets in July that differ from the throwback ones it typically wears with its classic uniforms. The Jets will pair it together with all-white jerseys and pants against the Green Bay Packers, who will wear their traditional home green on the road.

In the NFL "Rivalries" space, the Arizona Cardinals are the first to wear their design this season. Revealed last year, Arizona will rock it versus the Seattle Seahawks -- the same team they debuted it against in the previous campaign.
